newsitem.title: GERMANY: US soldiers to face rape court martial in Germany.
newsitem.headline: US soldiers to face rape court martial in Germany.

text.p: The U.S. army said on Tuesday it had referred charges against two soldiers, including rape and sodomy of female recruits at a training base in Germany, to the general courts-martial.
A statement by U.S. commanders based in Heidelberg said the charges, laid in February, were referred to the courts-martial on Monday and the soldiers would answer charges on April 11.
Sergeant First Class Julius Davis, based at the 440th Signal Battalion in Darmstadt, was accused on a number of charges including six counts of rape and one of forced sodomy.
Sergeant Paul Fuller, of the 77th Maintenance Company, Babenhausen in Germany, faces charges that included three counts of rape and three of sodomy.

The announcement came two months after the army removed First Sergeant George Watlington as head of the Darmstadt training centre, where 11 women soldiers said they were sexually assaulted or harassed by male sergeants from last November to January.

The two men, who were also accused of sexual harassment, have been held at the European Regional Confinement Facility, Coleman Barracks in Mannheim since February, partly for alleged interference in the investigation into them.

But the army said charges had not been referred to the courts-martial against Staff Sergeant Robert Robinson, of the 596th Maintenance Company in Darmstadt, who has been charged with maltreatment and fraternisation.
It said victims and witnesses had received support from the Victim-Witness Liason Program at Darmstadt.
The investigation in Germany followed a series of scandals at U.S. army bases in the United States, including accusations of sexual misconduct at the Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland.
